title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST requires that all left descendants have strictly smaller values and all right descendants have strictly larger values.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes in tree <= 10^4, -2^31 <= Node.val <= 2^31 - 1
hint: Node count up to 10^4 requires O(n) recursion, passing min and max valid bounds down to subtrees.
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively validates each node against min/max valid range boundaries (or checks strictly increasing order via in-order traversal) in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Tree BFS: Level-order traversal checking range limits works in O(n) time, but requires extra queue memory for range tuples. Not Binary Search: Binary search locates elements, but validating full tree structure requires inspecting all nodes. Not Monotonic Stack: Monotonic stack checks array monotonicity rather than hierarchical subtree value bounds.
